pool.text: Barcelona briefly became part of Napoleonic France.
Early industrialization began with steam-powered textile factories.
Catalan modernista architecture flourished, shaping Barcelona's artistic legacy.
Children comprised nearly 29% of Barcelona's population.
Barcelona became capital of autonomous Catalonia.
City was epicenter of Catalonia's Spanish Revolution.
Barcelona served as capital of the Second Spanish Republic.
Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany bombed Barcelona in March.
Fall of Barcelona triggered mass exodus to the French border.
Franco's death paved way for democratic demonstrations.
Over one million people demonstrated for Catalan autonomy.
Municipal elections were held again after the new constitution.
Spain joined the European Community and Barcelona won Olympic bid.
ETA car bomb at Hipercor killed 21 people.
Barcelona hosted the Summer Olympics, reshaping its global image.
Estació del Nord renovated for Olympic Games, now long‑distance bus terminus
Barcelona metropolitan area held 67% of Catalonia's industrial establishments
OBC opened its new Auditorium L'Auditori.
City began hosting the Bread & Butter urban fashion fair each summer
City Council launched the public Bicing bicycle‑sharing service
